description: Typed DAG of concepts/skills (Big Idea > objective > skill) with prerequisite and encompassing edges; lessons and items map to skills many-to-many.
user_value_why: Lets the app know what you know, what you're ready for, and why a lesson matters.
inputs: authored or generated concepts, edges with provenance
outputs: graph used by scheduler, paths, coverage, tutor routing
rationale: Merge B26's coded skill framework (CFL-1 style ids, lesson-to-skill tags, standards map) with BL's cross-domain course prereq/next-steps graph; primary = B26 skill granularity, add BL cross-domain edges and typed edge weights (FIRe encompassing).
recommended_source_pattern: merge: B26 Coding Skills Framework ids + BL course-graph edges + Math Academy encompassing weights
score_notes: ic=4: DAG integrity, provenance, editing UI; leverage/synergy=5: every adaptive feature reads it; privacy=1: no personal data.
refs: HC-21; HC-29; CH-36; ENG-21; SR-04; OBS-H

description: Curated ordered sequences of courses per subject with level labels (grade band or tier).
user_value_why: A clear 'where do I start / what's next' answer for a subject.
outputs: path page with recommended course order
rationale: Keep curated paths as the default face, but compute them as views over the skill graph so they can be re-ordered per learner; primary = B26 path UI, add knowledge-aware ordering (NEW).
recommended_source_pattern: merge: B26 learning paths rendered from concept_skill_graph
score_notes: differentiation=2: every course platform has paths; ic=2: a sorted view; comprehensibility=5.

description: Course > Level > Lesson > Exercise containers, with level-end review nodes and course-end practice.
user_value_why: Bite-size, finishable units with visible structure.
rationale: Observed directly (GameboardLessonNode / LevelReviewNode shapes); proven structure, trivial to model.
score_notes: use_frequency=5: every session; differentiation=2: standard; ic=2.

description: Courses and lessons carry versions; retired content moves to an always-available archive shelf with progress migrated across rename/merge/split.
user_value_why: You never lose a course or your progress mid-way (top complaint about Brilliant).
rationale: B26 has versionName/retiringOn but hides archives on desktop only and drops progress silently; improved version is cheap locally and fixes a trust failure.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 versionName/retiringOn fields, improved: archive on every surface + progress migration
score_notes: differentiation=4: Brilliant's documented failure; frequency=2: rarely visible; privacy=1.

description: Restore legacy breadth (science titles peaked around 2022-23 at ~19-20): physics (mechanics, E&M, waves/optics, gravitation, relativity, quantum), chemistry, biology, electronics, energy, info theory, quant finance, built from shared simulation generators.
user_value_why: Learn the sciences Brilliant retired: the user's stated core motivation.
inputs: domain syllabi skeletons (topic names only), generators per domain
rationale: Primary user goal. Brilliant retired breadth plausibly due to per-course content cost (about 2x exercise density in rebuilt courses); a generator-plus-eval engine makes breadth cheap. MVP ships one science domain (circuits/electricity); others roll out per roadmap.
recommended_source_pattern: BL 2019-2024 catalog as scope reference; content written fresh
score_notes: ic=5 and mb=4: each domain needs simulators + validators; differentiation=5: no current Brilliant equivalent; mvp_fit=3: one domain in MVP.

description: Per-domain Covered/Partial/Gap audit of skills; coverage = (C + 0.5P)/total; gaps link to 'generate lessons for this'.
user_value_why: See exactly which parts of a subject are missing and fill them on demand.
rationale: Cheap once the skill graph exists and powerful with generation, but not needed for the first learning loop. Promote when 3+ domains exist.
score_notes: differentiation=4 when tied to on-demand generation; mvp_fit=2; ic=2.

description: Tag skills to external frameworks (Common Core, NGSS, AP, SAT) and generate coverage pages.
user_value_why: Useful for school alignment and test prep.
rationale: Valuable for classrooms/test-prep, low value for a single self-directed learner. Promote if the user targets an exam.
score_notes: user_value=2, frequency=1, mvp_fit=1 for a personal app.

description: Scaffolded problem sequence: unlimited retries, tutor hints, See answer, Start over; attempts here never count toward mastery scores.
user_value_why: Mistakes feel safe, so learners experiment and build intuition.
rationale: Directly observed core mechanic; separating learning from measuring is Brilliant's key design insight.
score_notes: user_value/frequency/leverage=5: this IS the product; differentiation=5 vs answer-only quiz apps; ic=3.

description: End-of-lesson Skills Check: ~3 one-shot items in fresh configurations, no tutor, explanation only; scored in thirds.
user_value_why: An honest signal of whether the idea stuck, without punishing the learning phase.
inputs: variant items from the lesson's generators
rationale: Observed directly; cheap given generators; it is the clean evidence source for the knowledge model.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 check phase (observed) + HC-02 Skills Check
score_notes: leverage=5: only clean mastery evidence; ic=2 once generators exist.

description: Lesson authoring rule: pose 1-2 hands-on problems before any concept explanation; concept cards follow, then a takeaway.
user_value_why: Curiosity before vocabulary; learners discover the rule themselves.
rationale: Observed (concept page after two problems) and stated ('Action first. Theory later.'); productive-failure evidence supports it when prior knowledge exists. Add an adaptive switch to worked examples for brand-new learners (NEW, expertise reversal).

description: Within a lesson, one manipulative is reused with configurations that escalate difficulty, each targeting one misconception.
user_value_why: Deep understanding of one idea instead of shallow exposure to many.
rationale: Observed in Current Loops (switch topology escalation) and the blog (one core activity per course); maps directly onto generators.
score_notes: leverage=5: makes generated lessons coherent; ic=3: needs misconception-tagged radicals.

description: Short narrative/concept cards (text + diagram) and a one-sentence takeaway card with an animated diagram.
user_value_why: Names the idea after you've felt it; a memorable summary.
rationale: Observed; trivial to implement; required for every lesson.

description: Lesson types beyond standard: Explore / Apply / Derive lessons, end-of-level applied capstone 'Problem' lessons, narrative thought-experiment games, mini-courses.
user_value_why: Variety and transfer to real applications.
rationale: Legacy evidence only; valuable for advanced science courses. Promote with the second science domain.
recommended_source_pattern: BL Gravitational Physics Explore/Apply + Classical Mechanics capstones

description: One cross-subject problem per day with an 'insight' primer, multiple explanations after solving, and a browsable archive.
user_value_why: A low-friction daily habit hook that spans subjects.
inputs: generator pool across domains, date seed
rationale: Removed from Brilliant; cheap to restore once several domains have generators. Promote when 2+ domains are live.
recommended_source_pattern: BL Daily Challenges / Science Puzzles one-a-day

description: One typed interface for every interactive (render, getState, setState, validate, reset, describeForTutor, highlightTargets) with a declared input list plus a pure state-to-view function; widgets can subscribe to each other's state.
user_value_why: Every interactive is checkable, resettable, and tutor-visible by construction.
rationale: Brilliant's Diagrammar (inputs + pure function) and restricted problem APIs are what make generation, evals and Koji possible; this is the platform's spine.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 Diagrammar + restricted Elm problem APIs, re-expressed in TypeScript
score_notes: leverage/synergy/expansion=5; ic=4: careful API design up front; comprehensibility=3 (developer-facing).

description: Click/tap components inside a simulation (switches, gates, valves); the simulation is evaluated on Check and plays the outcome.
user_value_why: Learn by changing a real system and seeing the result.
rationale: Observed in Circuits; the template for all science domains.
score_notes: user_value=5, expansion=5 (reused by every science domain); ic=3.

description: Single/multi-select tiles (horizontal short options or vertical text options), with per-option result marks.
user_value_why: Fast answers where construction isn't the point.
rationale: Observed; trivial; needed for code-reading and concept checks. Distractors must come from misconception rules.

description: Math field with fraction/root templates, cursor navigation, multiple answer boxes with per-field feedback; parsed to MathJSON and checked by an expectations library.
user_value_why: Type real math answers on any device.
rationale: Brilliant wraps MathLive (observed via assets + engineer write-ups); MathLive is MIT and maintained.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 MathLive custom element > MathJSON > Elm expectations

description: Draggable objects with visible handles: tiles, weights on balances, blocks, pieces snapping to positions.
user_value_why: Physical intuition for abstract quantities.
rationale: Core to Solving Equations / Negative Numbers / mobiles; users report fragile drags, so build on Pointer Events with obvious handles.
score_notes: comprehensibility=3: handles hard to discover per reviews; ic=3.

description: Sliders bound to model parameters that update a diagram live (exploration) or set an answer.
user_value_why: See how a system responds as you vary one thing.
rationale: Long-standing (2018 release notes); trivial; essential for science exploration.

description: Drag points/lines on a coordinate plane (tangent lines, fits, vectors) with snapping and constraints.
user_value_why: Feel the math of functions and geometry.
rationale: Named by Brilliant (dragging a tangent line); JSXGraph or a thin custom SVG layer covers it.

description: Code view with editable slots filled from a token palette (no free typing); the program runs on Check with output console and execution pointer.
user_value_why: Mobile-friendly, always-parseable coding practice (predict, diagnose, fix).
rationale: Observed and elegant, but coding is not the first priority (science breadth is). Promote with the first CS course.

description: Full Python editor with Run, hidden tests, and repeated submissions (run/read, predict, debug, complete-the-logic).
user_value_why: Real programming practice offline.
rationale: Brilliant has 2,081 run-and-edit problems; important for CS but not MVP. CodeMirror 6 (mobile-capable), not Monaco.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 Thinking in Python editor; CodeMirror 6 + Pyodide

description: Drag-and-drop code blocks / pseudocode puzzles before text code.
user_value_why: Gentle on-ramp to programming.
rationale: Part of Brilliant's CS pedagogy; Blockly (Apache-2.0) available. v2 with CS track.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 Thinking in Code drag-and-drop; Blockly

description: Reorder or categorize items (steps of a proof, magnitudes, process stages).
user_value_why: Checks understanding of sequence and classification.
rationale: Cheap, generic primitive essential for custom-topic lessons where no simulator exists.
recommended_source_pattern: Perseus orderer/sorter taxonomy (reference only); B26 Order Logic

description: Explicit statechart per page: pristine > dirty > checked_correct | checked_incorrect > (try_again | see_answer) > continue; single primary button label from state; phase-aware (learn vs check).
user_value_why: Predictable, consistent flow on every screen.
outputs: UI state + event log the tutor reads
rationale: Observed in detail; an explicit statechart is the cleanest way to reproduce it and to expose an event log to the tutor.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 observed state machine; XState v5 (MIT)

description: Instant verdict on Check: green border + glow + short message when correct; amber (never red) when wrong; per-field marks; XP chip.
user_value_why: Know immediately, without shame.
rationale: Observed; trivial; amber-not-red is a deliberate low-shame choice to keep. Add a non-color cue (icon/text) for accessibility.

description: On Check, the simulation always plays out the learner's own configuration, including wrong ones (bulb stays dark, current takes the short path).
user_value_why: The wrong answer becomes its own explanation.
rationale: Directly observed; the strongest pedagogical pattern found; requires real simulators (not answer keys), which the science engine needs anyway.

description: Wrong states are classified against misconception rules; the hint names the specific rule violated (e.g. 'current takes a bulb-free path').
user_value_why: Feedback that diagnoses the actual misunderstanding.
rationale: Observed (state-specific Koji bubble); implement as deterministic rules per generator with optional LLM phrasing, so no hallucination risk.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 state-specific hint (observed) + Oppia misconception branches

description: Learn phase: Try again (keeps configuration), See answer, Start over; check phase: no retry; both phases: Why? opens a short explanation built from the solver's solution steps.
user_value_why: Control over how much help you take.
rationale: Observed; trivial once the state machine exists.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 Try again / See answer / Start over (observed)

description: Explanations at several depths: one-line Why, step-by-step worked view (staged animation on the same canvas), 'explain differently' alternatives, glossary popovers for terms.
user_value_why: Fixes the #1 content complaint: terse, puzzle-like explanations.
rationale: Primary = B26 'Why?' modal; add BL's multiple community explanations as generated alternatives and a step-by-step layer derived from the solver trace (never free LLM math).
recommended_source_pattern: merge: B26 Why? modal + BL voted alternative explanations (generated) + solver-step worked view
score_notes: user_value=5 per complaint frequency; ic=3; differentiation=4.

description: Flag icon on every item records generator id, seed and config; flagged items are quarantined, regenerated, and added to a regression set.
user_value_why: Bad content gets fixed and never comes back.
rationale: B26 only sends a report to staff; local closed loop with the generator pipeline is cheap and essential for AI content.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 flag/report (observed) improved into a local QA loop
score_notes: frequency=2; leverage=4 for content quality; ic=2.

description: Only check-phase, practice, and review items feed accuracy and mastery; learn-phase attempts are logged but unscored. First-attempt and eventual accuracy are stored separately.
user_value_why: Clean evidence for adaptivity; learning stays risk-free.
rationale: Observed arithmetic (83.3% = 5/6 assessed items) and K-5 docs (first-attempt vs eventual). Trivial and foundational.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 assessment accuracy model (observed) + K-5 first-attempt split

description: 10-15 item end-of-level review with no hints, mixing the level's skills; readiness signal.
user_value_why: Consolidates a level; reveals gaps before moving on.
rationale: Verified structure; cheap with generators; doubles as interleaved practice.

description: Optional gate to skip ahead: pass a level check using the same mastery criterion, which credits the skipped skills.
user_value_why: Don't waste time on what you already know.
rationale: Verified (Premium-only at Brilliant); soft gating is better than hard gating per mastery-learning evidence.

description: Short adaptive diagnostic over the skill graph that finds the knowledge frontier (outer fringe) and seeds per-concept ability.
user_value_why: Start at the right place on day one.
rationale: Primary = B26 signup diagnostic (opaque); add BL 5-difficulty probe per topic and KST outer-fringe selection to cut questions.
recommended_source_pattern: merge: B26 diagnostic + BL 5-level probe + KST fringe / Math Academy frontier
score_notes: frequency=1 (once per domain); leverage=5; privacy=2: knowledge profile is personal but stays local.

description: Visible per-concept mastery, uncertainty, last-retrieved date and next review; the user can correct it ('I know this').
user_value_why: Trust and agency: see and steer what the app believes about you.
rationale: Learner-model research says an open learner model matters as much as the estimator; Brilliant shows only lesson percentages.
score_notes: differentiation=5 vs Brilliant; ic=2; privacy=2 (local only).

description: Each lesson owns a practice set (scaffolds off) reachable from the completed node: [Practice] or [Redo].
user_value_why: Strengthen a specific lesson on demand.
rationale: Observed (nextPracticeSlug on every lesson node); trivial with generators.

description: Before the next new lesson, insert a short practice set retrieving the previous level's skills, chosen by the scheduler.
user_value_why: Retrieval before new learning, automatically.
rationale: Observed (Warm Up from previous level, home recommendation); becomes scheduler-driven instead of fixed.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 Warm Up insertion (observed) driven by FSRS

description: Produces fresh surface-varied variants of an item that keep the learning objective, including predict / diagnose / fix trios on one scenario.
user_value_why: Practice the skill, not the memorized item.
rationale: Verified (Brilliant's variation tool) and observed (Warm Up trio); every review and check item depends on it.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 variation tool + K-5 generator contract

description: Per-concept FSRS-6 memory card (not per item); reviews draw fresh variants; FIRe-style implicit credit flows through encompassing edges.
user_value_why: Long-term retention: Brilliant's biggest pedagogical gap (review sets only 'rolling out').
rationale: Primary = FSRS-6 via ts-fsrs (MIT) at concept level; take B26's 'personalized practice' and review-set intent; add FIRe credit propagation (Math Academy pattern).
recommended_source_pattern: merge: B26 personalized practice intent + FSRS-6 (ts-fsrs) + FIRe encompassing credit
score_notes: differentiation=5, ic=4 (no partial-review API in ts-fsrs); privacy=2 (local).

description: Mixed practice sets that deliberately pair confusable concepts (series vs parallel, molarity vs molality).
user_value_why: Learn to choose the right method, the skill that matters on real problems.
rationale: Brilliant tests it; strong evidence (d=0.83 RCT, g=0.42 meta); cheap with confusable edges.

description: Auto-collect missed items and allow manual bookmarks; review them later as a set.
user_value_why: Requested by users; personal review list.
rationale: User-requested; trivial; scheduler already covers most of the value. Promote in v1.x polish.

description: Per-concept ability theta (Elo/PFAE with uncertainty function), item difficulty frozen from generator features, EMA-based mastery with separate 'mastered' promotion after spaced retrieval.
user_value_why: The app knows what you know: the basis of dynamic lessons and paths.
outputs: theta, uncertainty, mastery state per concept
rationale: Brilliant describes 'user knowledge modeling' and next-problem prediction with population recommenders; single-user needs PFAE-Elo (no fitting) + EMA mastery. DKT is unsuitable without data.
recommended_source_pattern: merge: B26 knowledge modeling intent + Pelánek PFAE-Elo + EMA mastery criterion

description: Chooses the next lesson/review/item from outer fringe + due reviews, scored by urgency, compression, goal relevance, and interleave bonus; targets 75-85% predicted success.
user_value_why: Always the right next challenge: Brilliant's own data says this drives engagement more than game mechanics.
inputs: knowledge state, FSRS queue, goals, graph
rationale: Primary = B26 'predict optimal next problem X' intent; implement with KST fringe + FIRe-style compression + desirable-difficulty band.
recommended_source_pattern: merge: B26 next-problem prediction intent + KST outer fringe + Math Academy task selection

description: The scheduler inserts nodes into a course path (warm-ups, remediation, reviews) and skips mastered lessons; the path re-renders per learner.
user_value_why: Paths that bend to what you know: the user's requested 'dynamic lessons/paths'.
rationale: Observed hooks (gameboardV2 includeInsertions, Level.insertion); generalize them to full knowledge-aware path rendering.

description: When a learner stalls on X (2 halted attempts or repeated misconception), insert diagnostic items on X's highest-weight prerequisites up to 2 hops back, then return.
user_value_why: Fix the real gap instead of repeating the same lesson.
rationale: Brilliant only offers 'new practice problems' after a failed Skills Check; prerequisite remediation is a proven pattern (Math Academy, Oppia branches).
recommended_source_pattern: Math Academy remedial reviews + Oppia misconception branches

description: Free-text 'What do you want to learn?' mapped onto skill-graph nodes, returning a starting lesson/practice or a proposed path.
user_value_why: Learn what you need right now without knowing course names.
rationale: Verified (Ask Koji, math-only, web-only); extend to all subjects; same entry point as custom paths.
score_notes: ic=2 with LLM classification over a closed node list; privacy=2 (query may go to cloud LLM).

description: For any user-requested topic: retrieve open-textbook grounding, LLM proposes concepts and edges (structured output), external critics validate (DAG, textbook order, coverage), user edits the graph, a deterministic planner orders the path, and generators or generic primitives fill lessons.
user_value_why: Learn anything in STEM, not just what a catalog offers: the user's headline improvement and the route back to breadth.
outputs: editable concept graph + planned path + generated lessons
rationale: Primary = B26 Ask Koji routing (limited to existing math curriculum); extend with LLM graph proposal + deterministic planning (LLMs plan paths poorly: 29.5% pass) + external validation (LLM prerequisite flaws are invisible to LLM judges). Phased: path + generic-primitive lessons first, simulator lessons where a domain generator exists.
recommended_source_pattern: merge: B26 Ask Koji + LLM graph proposal + KST/topological deterministic planner
score_notes: ic=5: hardest feature; privacy=2: topic requests to cloud LLM; mvp_fit=3: ships late-MVP in reduced form.

description: Per-learner lesson variant: question-first when prerequisites are mastered, worked-example-with-backward-fading when brand new, collapsed explanations for experts.
user_value_why: Dynamic lessons: same objective, different route depending on what you know.
rationale: Strong evidence (expertise reversal, productive-failure prerequisites) but needs two authored/generated shapes per lesson. Promote after the base player and generators are stable.
recommended_source_pattern: Kalyuga rapid diagnostics + Renkl backward fading

description: Socratic tool-calling tutor grounded in live lesson state (widget state, attempt history, pauses) with per-concept tutor notes; never gives the answer before bottom-out; withdraws in check/assessment.
user_value_why: One-on-one help exactly where you're stuck.
inputs: lesson event log, item config + solver solution, tutor notes
rationale: Koji is Brilliant's 2026 centerpiece; the architecture (constrained LLM over deterministic lesson state, expert tutor notes, short replies) is documented. Safeguarded tutors avoid the 17% exam harm seen with unconstrained GPT.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 Koji: constrained LLM over deterministic lesson infrastructure
score_notes: ic=4, mb=4 (prompts/evals); privacy=3: lesson context to a cloud LLM unless local model; differentiation=5.
refs: ENG-02; ENG-03; ENG-04; ENG-31; PE-06; PG-04

description: On-demand pointing hint, then teaching hint (the principle), then bottom-out; only bottom-out counts as failure for mastery.
user_value_why: Help that keeps you doing the thinking.
rationale: Primary = B26 Koji 'asks instead of tells'; add Andes 3-level ladder semantics and the mastery accounting rule.
recommended_source_pattern: merge: B26 Koji Socratic policy + Andes pointing/teaching/bottom-out ladder
score_notes: ic=2: deterministic ladder with optional LLM phrasing.

description: Tutor tools that act on the interactive: highlight a component, draw/annotate, add a point, pose an intermediate question, swap to a simpler variant.
user_value_why: Show, don't tell: the tutor points at the exact thing.
inputs: tool calls referencing widget element ids
rationale: The 'graphical tutor' differentiator; needs describeForTutor/highlightTargets on every primitive. MVP: highlight + annotate; v1.x: rearrange, intermediate question.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 Koji highlight/annotate/rearrange; perfect-freehand (MIT) for ink

description: Every number/expression in tutor text is checked against the CAS/solver before display; tutor receives the solver's step-by-step solution in context.
user_value_why: A tutor that doesn't make math mistakes.
rationale: Brilliant claims accuracy 'technology' without detail; Khanmigo routes math through a calculator; Kestin RCT enriched prompts with expert solutions; wrong spoken numbers are 'catastrophic'.
recommended_source_pattern: Khan calculator routing + Kestin solution-in-context + Brilliant evals ethos

description: More help on new concepts, less as mastery rises; silent during check, review, and level-check items.
user_value_why: Builds independence, not dependency.
rationale: Verified Koji behavior and observed (no Koji in check phase); trivial policy.

description: Tutor speaks first on each page (what changed), reads problems aloud, accepts voice questions; local STT/TTS option.
user_value_why: Lowers the barrier to asking; accessibility for reading load.
rationale: Brilliant found voice 'essential' in testing, but it adds TTS/STT stacks and number-verification of speech. Kokoro (Apache-2.0) + whisper.cpp (MIT) viable locally. Promote after text tutor is stable.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 Koji voice (ElevenLabs) re-done with Kokoro + whisper.cpp

description: Animated tutor avatar with a state machine (idle, wave, nod, react-easy, react-struggle, celebrate) and speaking amplitude.
user_value_why: Students ask 'dumb' questions more freely with a character than a chat box.
rationale: Brilliant's testing favored a character; MVP uses a simple static/CSS avatar; full rig later (Rive authoring now needs a paid plan, so use Lottie/CSS/SVG).
recommended_source_pattern: B26 Koji Rive rig; re-implemented with SVG/Motion

description: Mute tutor chatter while keeping a minimal correct/incorrect verdict channel.
user_value_why: Focus without losing feedback.
rationale: Verified Koji behavior; trivial.

description: Typed, declarative lesson documents (pages of cards/problems referencing widget configs by id), validated by schema; diffable and LLM-generatable; optional branching edges.
user_value_why: Lessons that can be generated, validated, versioned, and adapted.
rationale: Brilliant drafts lessons in Camperdown (strict markup compiled to an app) and calls the lesson 'a layout engine that supports modules' with branching; a typed doc is the generation target.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 Camperdown markup + module layout engine

description: Per-skill generators that sample parameters within published ranges, compute answers deterministically, and expose difficulty radicals and misconception rules.
user_value_why: Unlimited correct practice; breadth becomes cheap.
rationale: Brilliant's game types are parameterized generators; the K-5 contract (rule-based per skill, fresh set each open, validity rules) is the default path.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 generator APIs + K-5 generator contract

description: LLM emits puzzle/lesson configs in an LLM-friendly representation under JSON-schema-constrained output (Claude structured outputs or Ollama format), never free-form UI.
user_value_why: New lessons for any topic in minutes.
rationale: Brilliant: representation redesign took gear-train generation from 0% to 93%; constrained decoding guarantees schema validity (not semantic validity).
recommended_source_pattern: B26 LLM content agent + Zod > JSON Schema > constrained decoding
score_notes: differentiation=5; privacy=2 (prompts to cloud unless local model).

description: Gate every generated item: math correctness (CAS simplify + numeric sampling), unique solvability (solver counting to 2), simulation consistency, impossible states, visual overlap, physical plausibility. Failures never reach the learner.
user_value_why: 100% correct content: 'almost right is catastrophically wrong'.
rationale: Brilliant's six eval dimensions; external checks are required because LLM self-correction doesn't fix reasoning errors.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 evals framework + MathCAMPS back-translation + SymPy dual check

description: Generated lessons/paths enter a preview queue where the user (as curator) can playtest, edit, accept, or reject before they enter the catalog; auto-accept allowed for eval-passing items in known generators.
user_value_why: Human-in-the-loop quality without a staff team.
rationale: Brilliant's human review rounds are essential; in a single-user app the learner is the curator, with auto-accept for proven generators.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 multi-round human review, adapted to a single user

description: Item difficulty (logit) computed from generator radicals and solver trace (steps, operation complexity, dependency depth); no population data needed.
user_value_why: Right-sized challenge from session one.
rationale: Required by the single-user knowledge model (co-estimating difficulty drifts under adaptive selection); solver-trace difficulty correlated r=0.95 with human solving time for Sudoku.

description: Distractors and wrong-state classifiers come from per-skill misconception rules, never free LLM text.
user_value_why: Wrong options that reveal real misunderstandings.
rationale: Brilliant skill guides list common mistakes; 49% of raw LLM MCQs are flawed, so rule-derived distractors are required.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 K-5 skill-guide misconceptions + K-5 'nearby choices' rule

description: Hand-checked exemplar items/lessons per generator used as few-shot anchors and regression tests.
user_value_why: Keeps generated content on-voice and on-standard.
rationale: Brilliant scales 'from hand-selected golden examples to AI generation at scale'.

description: Shared deterministic simulators: DC circuit nodal analysis, digital logic, statics/moments (mobiles, balances), gear trains, 2D ray optics, kinematics/orbit integrator, reaction kinetics/equilibrium, molecule validation (RDKit), qubit circuits.
user_value_why: Real behavior for every science domain; correctness and consequence feedback for free.
rationale: B26 has circuits, gears, mobiles, pool, optics, structures (Scientific Thinking games); BL breadth needs kinetics, orbits, molecules, quantum. Build in-house small solvers, cross-check with ngspice-WASM/Planck.js; avoid GPL CircuitJS and NC PhET. MVP = DC circuits + balance/statics.
recommended_source_pattern: merge: B26 puzzle-science game engines + BL domain coverage, implemented with small TS solvers
score_notes: ic=5, mb=4 overall (per-domain incremental); mvp_fit=3 (two simulators in MVP).
refs: CH-15; CH-29; ENG-19; OSS-42; OSS-43; OSS-51

description: Composable validators over MathJSON values with field-level messages (integer required, point on line, unique values, equivalent expression, unit-aware numeric tolerance).
user_value_why: Precise, fair checking of typed answers.
rationale: Brilliant's 'expectations' library over MathJSON; Compute Engine (MIT) isIdenticallyEqual() (symbolic + random-point sampling, may return undefined) for fast checks, SymPy-in-Pyodide as fallback when undefined, math.js for units.
recommended_source_pattern: B26 expectations library; Cortex Compute Engine + SymPy + math.js

description: Daily streak (3 assessed-or-learn problems or 1 lesson), lit at the moment of qualification; up to 2 streak charges auto-applied on a missed day; week strip.
user_value_why: A gentle daily habit with forgiveness.
rationale: Verified + observed; cheap; keep low-key (Brilliant's own data: game mechanics 'barely made a dent').

description: 15 XP per correct item, lesson (~+20) and practice (~+10) completion bonuses, no XP for same-day repeats.
user_value_why: Visible effort currency.
rationale: Observed values; trivial; secondary motivator.

description: 30-person weekly XP leaderboards, 10 tiers, top-10 promote / bottom-5 demote.
user_value_why: Social competition.
rationale: Out of scope: single-user local app has no other learners; multiplayer needs a server, accounts, and other people's data (privacy risk). Replace with personal_best_weeks.
score_notes: user_value=1 single-user; privacy=4 (other users' data); ic=4 (server).

description: Compete against your own past weeks (XP, mastery gained, reviews kept) instead of other people.
user_value_why: Competition without other users.
rationale: Cheap replacement for leagues; low value, so v1.x polish.

description: Declarative post-session event queue (lesson complete > XP > streak > charge), each skippable, collapsed to one line in focus mode.
user_value_why: Satisfying closure without nagging.
rationale: Observed chain; long-time users find heavy gamification 'twee', so make every step skippable and add focus mode.

description: Vertical trail of node pads per course (lesson, practice, review, check, inserted nodes) with status, color by domain, and a gold pad on completion.
user_value_why: See progress and what's next at a glance.
rationale: Observed; the visual home for dynamic paths.

description: Local notifications for daily practice and due reviews at a user-set time; no league/marketing reminders.
user_value_why: Nudges at the right time without spam.
rationale: Brilliant documents four categories but no reminder time; local reminders need the desktop shell. Promote when the Electron/PWA shell lands.

description: One toggle that hides gamification chrome, skips celebrations, and mutes sounds.
user_value_why: Serious learners keep the pedagogy without the confetti.
rationale: HN complaints about 'twee gamification'; trivial.

description: Append-only local log of every answer, hint request, reveal, pause, and session event with phase, item config hash, and timing.
user_value_why: Everything adaptive and every stat is derived from one honest record.
rationale: Brilliant logs 'every answer choice, hint click, and session event'; local-only storage keeps privacy risk contained.
score_notes: leverage=5; privacy=3: detailed behavioral data, mitigated by local-only storage.

description: Activities completed, assessment accuracy with week-over-week delta, problems solved chart, ranges (week/month/year/all), per-course lesson scores, skills learned.
user_value_why: See growth over time.
rationale: Observed (/you page); straightforward aggregates.

description: Natural-language weekly summary of what was learned and what's next.
user_value_why: A human-readable reflection prompt.
rationale: Observed but low value; trivial template version possible later.

description: Reset a lesson, a level ('reset from here'), or a whole course, all reversible via snapshots.
user_value_why: Restart cleanly without losing history forever.
rationale: Brilliant lacks whole-course reset and its level reset is irreversible; cheap with local snapshots. v1.x.

description: Supervised child accounts, family dashboards, classrooms, assignments, rostering.
user_value_why: Oversight for parents/teachers.
rationale: Out of scope for a single-user local app; requires multi-account server, rostering, and minors' data.
score_notes: privacy=5 (minors' data); ic=5; user_value=1 for this user.

description: All content, progress, and generation caches live in a local SQLite database; works fully offline except optional cloud-LLM features.
user_value_why: Own your data; learn anywhere; no paywall keys.
rationale: B26 requires a connection; BL once had offline mode; K-5 already stores progress on-device. Core user requirement ('locally').
recommended_source_pattern: BL offline mode + B26 K-5 device-only progress

description: One interface over Claude (cloud, best quality) and Ollama/llama.cpp (local, offline) with schema-constrained output, per-feature provider choice, and graceful degradation.
user_value_why: AI features work offline when needed and best-in-class when online.
rationale: Required by tutor, generation, and routing; Brilliant is 'fairly model agnostic'. Anthropic SDK must run server-side (browser use disabled by default).
recommended_source_pattern: Anthropic TS SDK + Ollama structured outputs behind one adapter
score_notes: privacy=3: cloud provider receives prompts (user opt-in, keys local); leverage=5.

description: Keyboard alternatives to every drag, screen-reader labels from describeForTutor, non-color verdict cues, adjustable text size, reduced motion, dark mode.
user_value_why: Usable by everyone, including when tired or on a phone.
rationale: Brilliant documents no accessibility features (App Store declares none); building it into the primitive contract is cheap now, expensive later.

description: Offline Python execution (Pyodide in a Web Worker) with output, traces, and hidden tests; SymPy available as CAS.
user_value_why: Run code and heavy math locally.
rationale: Needed for CS lessons and as authoritative CAS; heavy (200+ MB full distro). MVP uses Compute Engine for math; promote with CS track.

description: Optional sync of the local database between the user's devices.
user_value_why: Continue on phone where you left off on desktop.
rationale: B26 syncs via accounts; for a local app it needs a sync layer or file-based sync. Promote when a mobile client exists.

description: Accounts, 2-keys/day metering, Premium paywall, upsell screens, interstitial ads, gifts and family plans.
user_value_why: Revenue for Brilliant; friction for learners.
rationale: Out of scope and harmful to learning (keys cap practice; warm-ups cost keys); a personal local app has no monetization.

description: Per-concept reference page (definition, key formulas, worked example, links to lessons), separate from lessons; doubles as the tutor's retrieval corpus.
user_value_why: Look things up without replaying a lesson; reviewers keep their own notes today.
rationale: BL wiki survives read-only because reference outlives course rewrites; reviewers ask for reference material. Promote in v1.x with the tutor retrieval work.
recommended_source_pattern: BL community wiki (topic names only, fresh content)

description: The user writes or edits problems/lessons through the same typed format and eval gate.
user_value_why: Make your own practice; extend the catalog.
rationale: BL community authored 100k+ problems; for one user it's a power feature. v2.

description: Public discussion threads, solution voting, and solver counts.
user_value_why: Social learning.
rationale: Superseded: single-user app has no community; the value (alternative explanations) is merged into multi_depth_explanations.
